verdictRule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Measured: 0 blockers, 0 SHOULD-FIX, 1 advisory. Advisories do not block.
acceptanceGrade: ACCEPT-WITH-ONE-ADVISORY. Application-grade for what this artifact is — a measurement of fourteen EE classes against the live gate set — and expressly not a leftover closure.

scopeOfThisAcceptance.whatIsAccepted: That ten EE classes ride no live gate corpus and remain leftover-design; that EE-3a is discharged by DR-133 classes already named at G21 and G23 without itself being named there; that EE-6b, EE-7c and EE-7e are capable of riding DR-G09, DR-G14 and DR-G16 respectively, each with the gate's own owner and each with the naming recorded as owed; and that required-now stays 24 with no row proposed.
scopeOfThisAcceptance.whatIsNotAccepted: This ACCEPT does not close DR-117's leftover-design, does not make gates 2 or 3 hold, and does not make DR-117 eligible or SATISFIED. Ten classes have no obligation and three more are not yet named at the gates they could ride. DR-117 stays OPEN.
scopeOfThisAcceptance.whatItUnblocks: A later D-086 successor that would name EE-6b, EE-7c and EE-7e at their gates, and a separate decision about the ten that ride nothing.

priorErrorDisclosure.what: In the DR-117 v3 cycle I ACCEPTED an artifact whose EE-6b claimed the host refuses a trusted analyzer's undeclared socket. Codex rejected it correctly. That claim contradicted permission-truth-tables.v9, whose PT-NET-EGRESS is DISCLOSURE-ONLY and whose FX-2B asserts the ambient path succeeds, which is what proves the absence of enforcement. My refutation at the time wrongly generalised a pure-core law to a component process.
priorErrorDisclosure.consequenceForThisReview: EE-6b was the first thing I checked and I checked it against v5's own bytes and the truth-table posture rather than against my recollection.
priorErrorDisclosure.finding: The artifact is on the right side of it. Its EE-6b reason reads 'v5 already names G09 as leftover of DR-105 honesty, not confinement… Demonstrated prevention remains DR-128', which reproduces v5's own invariant — 'Component-originated PT-NET-EGRESS under ambient authority is DISCLOSURE-ONLY in the preview. The host neither observes nor prevents the ACT. A refused ASK is not a blocked ACT. This is honesty, not confinement.' Measured across the whole artifact, the only occurrences of prevent, confinement and honesty are in that one reason, and each is used to deny host prevention rather than assert it. Nothing here claims fail-closed enforcement.

EE-7e carries 'Release engineering + component/core/protocol/integration owners', while the live DR-G16 owner cell reads 'Release engineering + component/core/protocol/integration owners (owner cell made concrete 2026-08-13, C4)'. advisories.whyNotShouldFix: Nothing turns on it. The field is executionObligationOwnerToday rather than a field labelled verbatim, so a characterisation is defensible, and the omitted clause is a date annotation rather than an owner. I record it because the other two are exact, which makes the third look like an oversight rather than a choice, and because a later reviewer comparing to file 08 will hit the difference and have to work out which it was.

consideredAndDeclined.item: executionObligationOwnerToday asserts a present-tense owner for three classes not yet named at those gates
consideredAndDeclined.observation: The field name says today, and the naming is owed rather than done. I charged exactly this shape at the DR-131 join v1.
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: What I charged at DR-131 v1 was the present-tense claim with no owed act recorded; the repair there was to set the fields to none because that class had no distinct obligation. Here all three riding classes carry an owedLater in the same object, recording that a later D-086 successor may name them and that this join does not. That is the shape I accepted at the DR-133 join v6, where riding classes carried the gate's owner alongside an owedLater. Read as a whole, the field names the owner of the gate that exists today, and the owedLater says the class is not yet named at it. Consistency with my own accepted precedent requires declining.

consideredAndDeclined.item: The class entries carry reasons rather than verbatim quotations of v5's invariant, input and pass
consideredAndDeclined.observation: The DR-131 join carried verbatim name, input and pass for every class, and I verified twenty-four such fields there.
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: The prompt for this subject does not raise verbatim reproduction as an attack, unlike the DR-131 join prompt, and the artifact pins v5 at its digest with its role stated. I verified each reason against v5's own owner and existingGate fields class by class instead, and all of them hold. Requiring a quotation format the coordinator did not ask for would be inventing a requirement.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with one advisory. Thirteen attacks run, one landed and it is advisory-grade. Read the scope before recording: this is a measurement, not a closure. Ten of DR-117's fourteen EE classes remain leftover-design, three more are only capable of riding gates they are not yet named at, gates 2 and 3 do not hold, and DR-117 stays OPEN. Custody is clean: ae20b25f at 0444 unmoved, HEAD never left a6081c6, file 08 at the 6d593a11 pin the artifact itself carries, and D-154's application byte-identical to what it consented to. This is the row where I got a review wrong — I accepted DR-117 v3 on an EE-6b claim that the host refuses a trusted analyzer's undeclared socket, which contradicted permission-truth-tables.v9, and Codex rejected it correctly. So EE-6b was the first class I opened here, and I read v5's own bytes before the join's account of them. The artifact is on the right side of it: its EE-6b reason reproduces v5's invariant that component-originated PT-NET-EGRESS is DISCLOSURE-ONLY, that the host neither observes nor prevents the ACT, that this is honesty and not confinement, and that demonstrated prevention remains DR-128. Measured across the whole file, the only occurrences of prevent, confinement and honesty sit in that one reason, each denying host enforcement rather than asserting it. The rest holds too. Fourteen classes in v5 and fourteen in the join, same ids, partitioned into ten leftover, one discharged and three riding with no overlap or omission. Each reason tracks v5's own owner and existingGate statement — G21 is not a sandbox, G01 through G05 do not own analyze egress, DR-101 owns core inventory only, the second-role refusal is the D-002 and DR-118 role-list decision rather than G13. EE-3a uses the discharged-not-named formulation that repaired the DR-131 join, from the start rather than after a rejection. All three riding classes carry an owedLater recording the D-086 successor that would name them, which is the half whose absence I charged at the DR-131 join v1 and the shape I accepted at the DR-133 join v6. Required-now is 24, matching the live condition-4 cell after D-154, and no row is proposed. The advisory is that EE-7e's owner string is the live DR-G16 owner cell minus its dating parenthetical, where the other two are byte-exact — the owner identified is right, but the inconsistency is worth closing. One further item is recorded as considered and declined: the executionObligationOwnerToday field asserts a present-tense owner for classes not yet named, which I charged at the DR-131 join v1 and decline here because each class carries the owed naming act in the same object, matching the precedent I accepted at DR-133.
